subject: Genetics
title: Direct-to-Consumer Testing
description: A fast breakdown of Direct-to-Consumer Testing for builders.

hook.text: Spit in a tube, mail it off, and learn your ancestry and disease risks. 40 million people have done this.

buildup.text: 23andMe launched in 2006 at $999. By 2023, tests cost $99. Price drops democratized genetic information.

discovery.text: Consumer tests read about 700,000 DNA positions—not the full genome, but enough to estimate ancestry and some risks.

twist.text: The data has value beyond the buyer. 23andMe sold access to its database to drug companies for research.

climax.text: Police used consumer DNA databases to catch the Golden State Killer. Privacy met public safety, and privacy lost.

punchline.text: You paid for the test. Your data paid it forward.

quiz.question: How many people have used direct-to-consumer DNA tests?
